                    Public Utility Commission of Texas

                                      Memorandum

TO:            Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson
               Commissioner Kathleen Jackson
               Commissioner Courtney K. Hjaltman
               Commissioner Morgan Johnson
               Commissioner Patrick Rhode

FROM:          Jessie Horn, Sr. Counsel, Rules and Projects Division

DATE:          September 3, 2026

RE:            September 11, 2026 Open Meeting – Agenda Item No. 24
               Project No. 58481, Rulemaking to Implement Large Load Interconnection Standards
               Under PURA §37.0561


       Please find attached to this memorandum Commission Staff’s recommended adoption
order in the above-referenced project for consideration at the September 11, 2026, Open Meeting.
Commission staff’s recommended adoption order would adopt new 16 Texas Administrative
Code (TAC) §25.194, relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards.

       The purpose of the new rule is to implement Public Utility Regulatory Act §37.0561, as
enacted by Senate Bill 6 during the Texas 89th Legislature, Regular Session. Commission
Staff’s recommended adoption order requires a large load customer, before the large load
customer can be included in an ERCOT interconnection study, to execute an intermediate
agreement, provide certain disclosures, and post financial security in the amount $50,000 per
megawatt. The new rule also requires a large load customer to execute a standard large load
agreement, update its disclosures, post financial security, and pay contribution in aid of
construction for direct interconnection costs. Additionally, the new rule sets forth the
consequences of withdrawing all or a portion of requested peak demand or contracted peak demand
and the consequences for providing false or inaccurate information. Finally, the new rule sets forth
the terms for the return of financial security to a large load customer that energizes.

       Commission Staff recommends the Commission adopt the order attached to this
memorandum.
                                             PROJECT NO. 58481

      RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                        §       PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
      LARGE LOAD                                     §
      INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS                      §                     OF TEXAS
      UNDER PURA §37.0561                            §


                                      (STAFF RECOMMENDATION)


                               ORDER ADOPTING NEW 16 TAC §25.194


 1   The Public Utility Commission of Texas (commission) adopts new 16 Texas Administrative Code

 2   (TAC) §25.194, relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards, with changes to the proposed

 3   text as published in the March 27, 2026 issue of the Texas Register (51 TexReg 1942). The new

 4   rule implements Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA) §37.0561 as enacted by Senate Bill (SB)

 5   6 during the Texas 89th Regular Legislative Session. The new rule requires a large load customer,

 6   before the large load customer can be included in an ERCOT interconnection study, to execute an

 7   intermediate agreement, provide certain disclosures, and post financial security in the amount

 8   $50,000 per megawatt (MW). The new rule also requires a large load customer to execute a

 9   standard large load agreement (SLLIA), update its disclosures, post financial security, and pay

10   contribution in aid of construction (CIAC) for direct interconnection costs. Additionally, the new

11   rule sets forth the consequences of withdrawing all or a portion of requested peak demand or

12   contracted peak demand and the consequences for providing false or inaccurate information.

13   Finally, the new rule sets forth the terms for the return of financial security to a large load customer

14   that energizes. This section is adopted under Project Number 58481.

15

16   The commission received written comments on the proposed section from Advanced Power

17   Alliance and American Clean Power Association (APA and ACP); AEP Texas Inc. (AEP); Agentic

 3   Country Electric Cooperative, Inc., South Texas Electric Cooperative, Inc. (collectively, TSP

23   Cooperatives, Inc. (TEC); Texas Energy Buyers Alliance (TEBA); Texas Industrial Energy
      Project No. 58481            (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                  Page 3 of 280


 1   Consumers (TIEC); Texas-New Mexico Power Company (TNMP); Texas Oil & Gas Association

 2   (TXOGA); Texas Public Policy Foundation (TPPF); Texas Public Policy Association (TPPA);

 3   City of Bryan; Thor Equities; Tract Holding Company I, LLC (Tract); Trammell Crow Company

 4   (TCC); Vistra Corporate Services Company (Vistra); Voltus; Wind Energy Transmission Texas,

 5   LLC (WETT), Cross Texas Transmission, LLC (CTT), Lone Star Transmission, LLC (Lone Start),

 6   and Sharyland Utilities, LLC (Sharyland) (Collectively, Joint TSPs); and Zachary Butler, Blind

 7   Mice Labs (Zachary Butler).


 8   General Comments


 9   Loads included in batch zero interconnection study

10   Agentic, EH2, HIF, Monarch, Skybox, Targa, TEBA, and Tract recommended modifying the

11   proposed rule to address a large load customer’s eligibility for inclusion in Batch Zero as either

12   firm load or studied load. Black Mountain Power, Targa, and Vistra recommended modifying the

13   proposed rule to prioritize certain types of loads for inclusion in Batch Zero.


14   Commission Response

15   The commission declines to adopt commenters’ recommendation to address a large load

16   customer’s eligibility for inclusion in the batch zero interconnection study as either firm load

17   or studied load; and declines to adopt commenters’ recommendation to prioritize certain

18   types of loads for inclusion in the batch zero interconnection study. Neither is necessary

19   because Planning Guide Revision Request (PGRR) 145, which was approved by the

20   commission on June 18, 2026, addresses eligibility and study requirements for batch zero

21   load.
      Project No. 58481           (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                   Page 4 of 280


 1   Changes to PGRR 145

 2   EH2, Eolic, Landmark and EcoPartner, and Monarch recommended modifying the proposed rule

 3   to direct ERCOT to make changes to PGRR 145.


 4   Commission Response

 5   The commission declines to adopt EH2, Eolic, Landmark and EcoPartner, and Monarch’s

 6   recommendation to modify the adopted rule to direct ERCOT to make changes to PGRR

 7   145. PGRR 145 was approved by the commission on June 18, 2026; therefore, changes to

 8   PGRR 145 are moot. Additionally, PGRR 145 establishes the eligibility criteria for large load

 9   customers to be included in the batch zero interconnection study as either base load or

10   studied load and the process for the batch zero interconnection study. The adopted rule does

11   not address these issues.


12   Loads studied in the Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP)

13   PBPA requested the commission clarify how the proposed rule and batch process create a path for

14   interconnection for all loads that supported the need for the PBRP, including those below 75 MW.

15   PBPA recommended the proposed rule and batch process include appropriate safeguards to ensure

16   transmission infrastructure is made available to serve oil and gas loads that formed the basis for

17   the PBRP.


18   Commission Response

19   The commission declines to adopt PBPA’s recommendation to clarify how the proposed rule

20   and batch process create a path for interconnection for loads that were studied in the PBRP,

21   including those below 75 MW. The interconnection path for loads below 75 MW is outside

22   the scope of the adopted rule. The commission also declines to modify the adopted rule to
      Project No. 58481           (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                   Page 5 of 280


 1   ensure transmission infrastructure is made available to serve oil and gas loads studied in the

 2   PBRP. Neither is necessary. PGRR 145 addresses eligibility for inclusion in the batch zero

 3   interconnection study. All other large load customers must comply with the adopted rule for

 4   inclusion in a future interconnection study. The standards in the adopted rule apply equally

 5   to all large load customers.


 6   Financial commitments for studied loads included in Batch Zero

 7   For batch zero loads that do not qualify as “base load”—i.e., projects that have not yet satisfied

 8   ERCOT Planning Guide Sections 9.4 and 9.5 through completion of required studies, execution

 9   of interconnection agreements, and demonstration of financial commitment—Skybox

10   recommended ensuring that any new financial requirements are calculated on a net basis, with full

11   credit given to amounts already posted with or paid to the applicable distribution service provider

12   (DSP) or transmission service provider (TSP).


13   Commission Response

14   The commission declines to adopt Skybox’s recommendation to ensure that any new

15   financial requirements required of a studied load in the batch zero interconnection study be

16   calculated on a net basis with full credit given to amounts already posted with or paid to the

17   applicable DSP or TSP. Instead, the commission modifies the adopted rule to ensure that a

18   letter of credit or guaranty serving as financial security is returned to a large load customer

19   that is included in the batch zero interconnection study and cash collateral serving as

20   financial security is returned or credited based on the large load customer’s election and

21   notice to the applicable DSP or TSP. The commission also modifies the adopted rule to

22   require all loads eligible for inclusion in the batch zero interconnection study to execute a

23   Standard Large Load Interconnection Agreement (SLLIA) with new obligations to post
      Project No. 58481            (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                  Page 6 of 280


 1   financial security. This creates uniform treatment for large load customers that have not

 2   energized as of the effective date of the adopted rule and ensures that the circumstances

 3   allowing the DSP or TSP to draw down on the financial security contemplate payment for

 4   outstanding amounts owed as described in the adopted rule thus striking a balance between

 5   ensuring that large load customers are not posting double the financial security and

 6   protecting ratepayers against stranded infrastructure costs.


 7   If applicable

 8   Constellation and LCRA recommended modifying the phrase “interconnecting DSP or

 9   interconnecting TSP” throughout the rule to state “interconnecting DSP or, if applicable,

10   interconnecting TSP” to avoid inference that the entity is discretionary.


11   Commission Response

12   The commission declines to adopt Constellation and LCRA’s recommendation to modify the

13   phrase “interconnecting DSP or interconnecting TSP” throughout the rule to state

14   “interconnecting DSP or, if applicable, interconnecting TSP” because the division of

15   responsibility is best addressed in a separate rulemaking to adopt a SLLIA.


16   Non-refundable financial security

17   Black Mountain Power, Skybox, TCC, and TEBA recommended modifying the proposed rule to

18   revise the non-refundability of financial security.

19

20   Specifically, Black Mountain Power recommended revising the proposed rule to tie financial

21   exposure to meaningful milestones. Skybox recommended that refund and credit calculations

22   should be applied after giving effect to first-dollar crediting of existing financial security and
      Project No. 58481            (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                      Page 7 of 280


 1   CIAC; no portion of the required financial commitment should be subject to forfeiture for

 2   undelivered capacity or delay driven deferrals outside the customer’s control; and DSPs and TSPs

 3   should retain the ability to require incremental financial commitments only to the extent necessary

 4   to cover actual interconnection related costs associated with delivered capacity.

 5

 6   TCC recommended modifying the proposed rule to provide that the financial security balance must

 7   be refunded when the large load customer “reaches and sustains the contracted level of operation”

 8   because the 5-year period is excessive and inconsistent with industry practice.

 9

10   TEBA opposed the imposition of non-refundable security before any load studies occurred and

11   before any transmission is confirmed to be available, or when it might materialize. TEBA

12   recommended that non-refundability is appropriate when a developer has elected to move forward

13   with inclusion in a transmission plan that incorporates their loads and should be limited to

14   protecting other customers from paying for costs incurred by the utility on their behalf if the

15   developer does not ultimately move forward. TEBA recommended that all financial security be

16   refunded upon energization and the load transitions to minimum transmission charges. TEBA

17   noted that the process is unclear for exercising corporate guarantee payments for projects that do

18   not move forward in the process. To address this, TEBA recommended that the utility directly

19   invoice a developer who leverages a parental guarantee if their project is cancelled.


20   Commission Response

21   The commission adopts Black Mountain Power, Skybox, and TEBA’s recommendation to

22   revise the non-refundability of financial security. Specifically, the commission modifies the

23   adopted rule to allow return of all financial security after collection of outstanding amounts
      Project No. 58481            (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                   Page 8 of 280


 1   owed if a large load customer withdraws its interconnection request before the

 2   interconnection study begins and authorizes the return of financial security after: (1)

 3   collection of outstanding amounts owed and (2) subtraction of 20% of the financial security

 4   associated with transmission capacity allocated if a large load customer withdraws its

 5   interconnection request after ERCOT has allocated transmission capacity. The commission

 6   also adopts TEBA’s recommendation to allow the interconnecting DSP or TSP to invoice a

 7   large load customer if its project is cancelled. However, the commission modifies the adopted

 8   rule to allow the interconnecting DSP or TSP to invoice the large load customer for

 9   outstanding amounts owed regardless of what manner of financial security was posted.


10   Limitations of financial security

11   CenterPoint recommended that proposed §25.194(g) through (i), each of which requires the

12   interconnecting utility to draw down on financial security in different circumstances, are in

13   conflict. Once financial security is drawn down is under one of these subsections, it will no longer

14   be available for use under any of the other subsections.


15   Commission Response

16   The commission agrees with CenterPoint that once financial security is drawn down it is no

17   longer available for use under other circumstances. However, the commission disagrees that

18   the adopted rule results in a conflict by requiring the interconnecting DSP or TSP to draw

19   down on financial security in different circumstances because the identified circumstances

20   are mutually exclusive.
      Project No. 58481             (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                 Page 9 of 280


 1   Framework for flow of financial security obligations

 2   APA and ACP, BKV, CloudHQ, CPV, HEN, Infinium, Intersect Power, OCSC and TCAP, Oncor,

 3   Rowan, Schaper Energy, Tesla, and TPPA recommended modifying the framework for flow of

 4   financial security commitments and obligations.

 5

 6   Specifically, APA and ACP recommended modifying the proposed rule to: (1) reduce the amount

 7   that is not refundable from 80% to no more than 10% with the remainder refunded if the

 8   developer’s withdrawal does not adversely affect other requests in the cluster; (2) allow the non-

 9   refundable portion to be held until the end of the study process and used only to fund underfunded

10   upgrades or restudies; and (3) allow a one-time transfer mechanism such as the one used in the

11   Southwest Power Pool’s Consolidated Planning Process.

12

13   BKV recommended a framework whereby: (1) intermediate-stage security is released when

14   security is posted under an interconnection agreement, unless the customer elects to carry it

15   forward for other financial obligations; (2) CIAC and equipment-related payments are fully

16   creditable and not duplicative of other security requirements; (3) additional financial obligations

17   are limited to incremental, project-specific costs not already secured or funded; and (4) to the

18   extent multiple financial instruments are retained, expressly require transparent accounting and

19   appropriate crediting across categories.

20

21   CPV recommended applying the interconnection fee to financial security requirements after

22   execution of the interconnection agreement. CPV also recommended requiring financial security

23   only after the results of a feasibility study are available.
      Project No. 58481            (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                  Page 10 of 280


 1

 2   CloudHQ recommended modifying the proposed rule to require only one form of financial security

 3   at the interconnection agreement phase. HEN recommended aligning the financial obligations with

 4   expected system use and avoiding duplicative recovery for the same MW of demand.

 5

 6   Infinium recommended the commission clarify whether financial obligations arising under the

 7   interconnection agreement are additive to, or inclusive of obligations arising under the

 8   intermediate agreement stage.

 9

10   Intersect Power and Schaper Energy generally recommended: (1) clarifying that all financial

11   commitments are creditable on a dollar-for-dollar basis across stages and categories; (2) replacing

12   the non-refundable interconnection fee with a creditable financial security construct, under which

13   any security posted at the intermediate stage is maintained and applied on a dollar-for-dollar basis

14   to actual project costs (including CIAC, equipment, and system upgrades), with any additional

15   security limited to incremental, project-specific cost exposure; (3) confirming that CIAC and

16   equipment-related payments are not duplicative of other security requirements; and (4)

17   maintaining independent security for system upgrades only where stranded cost risk is project-

18   specific and demonstrable.

19

20   OCSC and TCAP recommended clarifying the particular flow of funds among the fee categories

21   and the extent to which a large load customer will be refunded for financial security posted as part

22   of the intermediate agreement if ERCOT does not award that customer the full amount of its

23   requested peak demand and that customer thus decides to withdraw its requested peak demand.
      Project No. 58481            (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order               Page 11 of 280


 1   OCSC and TCAP also recommended including all categories of fees under one subsection so that

 2   they are readily available and easier to review.

 3

 4   Oncor recommended that the commission allow the required financial commitments in the

 5   interconnection agreement phase to overlap, not stack.

 6

 7   Rowan recommended modifying the adopted rule to provide that upon execution of the

 8   interconnection agreement, the interconnecting DSP or TSP must credit financial security posted

 9   under the intermediate agreement to financial security and obligations arising from the

10   interconnection agreement. If the security posted under the intermediate agreement exceeds the

11   amount required under the interconnection agreement, the excess must be refunded within 60 days.

12

13   Tesla recommended modifying the proposed rule to apply the deposit paid at the intermediate

14   agreement stage to other project costs and financial postings as the customer moves through the

15   interconnection process.

16

17   TPPA recommended modifying the rule to base the intermediate financial security requirement on

18   75% instead of 100% of requested peak demand and assess the remaining 25% during the

19   interconnection phase.


20   Commission Response

21   The commission adopts commenters’ recommendation to revise the framework for financial

22   security. Accordingly, the commission modifies the adopted rule in a manner that allows

23   financial security commitments and obligations to overlap rather than stack; clarifies the
      Project No. 58481           (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                Page 12 of 280


 1   flow through of various financial security requirements; and clarifies the circumstances

 2   under which financial security must be returned to a large load customer.

 3

 4   Specifically, the adopted rule is modified to allow cash collateral posted as financial security

 5   under an intermediate agreement to be credited to the financial security requirements for

 6   significant equipment or services. A letter of credit or guaranty provided under an

 7   intermediate agreement must be returned.

 8

 9   The commission also clarifies that, at the end of the batch study, an interconnecting DSP or

10   TSP must return financial security to a large load customer that is allocated 0 MW of

11   transmission capacity after collecting outstanding amounts owed. A large load customer that

12   withdraws its interconnection request but was allocated transmission capacity may receive

13   the balance of its financial security after the interconnecting DSP or TSP collects payment

14   for outstanding amounts owed and subtracts 20% of the financial security associated with

15   the allocated transmission capacity.

16

17   The commission also modifies the adopted rule to remove the interconnection fee under the

18   SLLIA. At the time the SLLIA is executed, the large load customer must post financial

19   security in an amount that is the greater of $50,000 per MW of the contracted peak demand

20   or the costs allocated to the large load customer for system upgrades as a result of an

21   interconnection study. A large load customer may elect to apply cash collateral posted as

22   financial security under an intermediate agreement as a credit towards the financial security

23   requirements under a SLLIA.
      Project No. 58481           (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order              Page 13 of 280


 1

 2   The interconnecting DSP or TSP must invoice the large load customer for direct

 3   interconnection costs as those costs are incurred; and the interconnecting DSP or TSP must

 4   return 20% of financial security when the large load customer energizes and the remainder

 5   ratably in 20% increments as the large load customer meets the milestones identified in the

 6   customer’s SLLIA for meeting its obligation to pay the large load minimum billing demand

 7   described in §25.193, relating to Distribution Service Provider Transmission Cost Recovery

 8   Factor (TCRF), for the set period of time described in §25.193.

 9

10   The commission determines that this framework best balances support for business

11   development and the need to minimize the potential for stranded infrastructure costs.


12   Tie payment of financial security to development milestones

13   Mission Power and PPM recommended modifying the proposed rule to increase financial security

14   requirements as a project progresses through commercial development milestones. The City of

15   Bryan stated that it supports a staged approach to financial commitments and a refundability

16   framework tied to energization milestones.


17   Commission Response

18   The commission declines to adopt Mission Power and PPM’s recommendation to modify the

19   adopted rule to increase financial security requirements as a project progresses through

20   commercial development milestones. Requiring financial security at the intermediate

21   agreement stage ensures that a large load customer has access to the necessary capital to see

22   a project through to energization. Additionally, the risk for stranded infrastructure costs is
      Project No. 58481             (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                   Page 14 of 280


 1   present when the large load customer is included in ERCOT’s forecast for transmission

 2   planning, which going forward will be at the time that the SLLIA is executed.


 3   Address cost causation and recovery in Project No. 58484

 4   TPPA recommended addressing cost causation and recovery in Project No. 58484, Evaluation of

 5   Transmission Cost Recovery, but was supportive of the fees and financial security proposed

 6   throughout the rule if addressed here. Additionally, if the interconnection fee and financial security

 7   requirements in the proposed rule are retained, TPPA recommended that the commission clearly

 8   state that adoption of these provisions does not materially resolve or address the issues under

 9   consideration in Project No. 58484.


10   Commission Response

11   The commission agrees with TPPA that transmission cost recovery should be addressed in a

12   separate rulemaking project. Therefore, the commission modifies the adopted rule to remove

13   the requirement that an interconnecting DSP or TSP apply retained financial security as an

14   offset to rate base and removes the prohibition for an interconnecting DSP or TSP to recover

15   direct interconnection costs in regulated rates. The commission will address transmission

16   cost recovery in Project No. 58000, Rulemaking to Update Wholesale and IOU Retail

17   Transmission Cost Recovery in the ERCOT Region.


18   Tie financial security to cost responsibility

19   APA and ACP recommended tying the financial security amounts to a developer’s identified cost

20   responsibility, once established in Project No. 58484, Evaluation of Transmission Cost Recovery.

21   This ensures that each interconnecting entity bears the direct consequences of its actual system

22   impacts and incentivizes timely withdrawal by projects whose upgrades would impose
      Project No. 58481            (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                  Page 15 of 280


 1   disproportionate or uneconomic costs on the system. APA and ACP also recommended that

 2   financial security for interconnection facilities sand network upgrades should remain “at-risk” only

 3   to the extent necessary to cover actual underfunded upgrades or restudies caused directly by

 4   developer withdrawals. If the load proceeds as expected, security should be refunded promptly

 5   once the load reaches commercial operation.


 6   Commission Response

 7   The commission declines to adopt APA and ACP’s recommendation to address financial

 8   security amounts in Project No. 58484. PURA §37.0561(h) requires that the large load

 9   interconnection standards include uniform financial commitment requirements for the

10   development of transmission infrastructure needed to serve a large load customer.

11   Therefore, it is appropriate to address financial security amounts in the adopted rule, which

12   also sets forth the requirements for a SLLIA. The commission disagrees that financial

13   security should be returned once the load reaches commercial operation because the risk for

14   stranded infrastructure remains even after commercial operation begins. Accordingly, the

15   commission also modifies the adopted rule to specify that additional financial security

16   relating to the large load minimum billing demand may be required.


17   Allocate the cost of 765-kV STEP and associated projects to large loads

18   TPPF recommended allocating the costs of the 765 kilovolt (765-kV) Strategic Transmission

19   Expansion Plan (STEP) and associated projects to large loads. TPPF reasoned that loads above 75

20   MW are the only reason systemwide demand may rise high enough over the next 10-15 years to

21   justify the 765-kV lines.
      Project No. 58481           (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                  Page 16 of 280


 1   Commission Response

 2   The commission declines to adopt TPPF’s recommendation to allocate the costs of the 765-

 3   kV STEP and associated projects because cost allocation for specific projects is outside the

 4   scope of this rulemaking. The purpose of this rulemaking is to establish uniform,

 5   standardized interconnection standards for large load customers.


 6   Minimum transmission/minimum demand charge

 7   AEP, CCNG, Google, Lancium, & TotalEnergies, LCRA, Oncor, TCC, TEBA, and Thor

 8   recommended the commission modify the proposed rule to require a large load customer to pay a

 9   capacity-based charge.

10

11   Additionally, CCNG recommended adding a new subsection requiring a large load customer to

12   pay a minimum transmission charge of no less than 50 percent of the customer’s contracted peak

13   demand for a period of five years. CCNG reasoned that this approach is more equitable than

14   requiring large load customers to pay financial security for system upgrades.

15

16   Google, Lancium, and TotalEnergies recommended adding a new provision that requires a DSP to

17   assess a transmission demand charge to large load customers for a period of five years based on a

18   percentage of the customer’s contracted peak demand. Google, Lancium, and TotalEnergies

19   further recommended modifying proposed §25.194(f)(10) to replace the requirement that a large

20   load customer post financial security for system upgrades with a statement that the interconnection

21   agreement should state that the large load customer will pay the minimum transmission charge

22   following energization.

23
      Project No. 58481             (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                    Page 17 of 280


 1   HEN recommended that any minimum demand or take-or-pay construct should be narrowly

 2   tailored to reflect actual reserved system capacity and applied only where necessary. HEN

 3   reasoned that broad application risks creating a “pay-for-readiness” model that requires large load

 4   customers to pay for transmission capacity regardless of actual usage discouraging private

 5   investment and distorting efficient market outcomes.

 6

 7   Oncor recommended requiring interconnection agreements to include a contractual commitment

 8   in which interconnecting large loads over 200 MW agree to pay rates proportional to the amount

 9   of capacity that they contract for, regardless of usage, for at least 10 years after interconnection.

10

11   If the proposed rule is modified to implement a minimum demand charge, OPUC recommended

12   that the commission: (1) include cost recovery methods, including penalty fees, if the large load

13   customer ceases operations before the end of ten or fifteen years; (2) consider the long asset life

14   of transmission infrastructure and the depreciation value in calculating the minimum demand

15   charge and payment period; (3) prohibit utilities from adding provisions to their tariffs or contracts

16   that result in large load customers paying less costs than they would under any minimum demand

17   charge rule; and (4) not presume load growth will continue at the same unprecedented rate long-

18   term in determining the minimum demand charge structure.

19

20   TCC recommended the commission establish a minimum demand charge in a contested case. Thor

21   recommended replacing the interconnection fee with a minimum demand charge of no less than

22   50% of contracted peak demand for five years.
      Project No. 58481            (Staff Recommendation) Adoption Order                  Page 18 of 280


 1   Commission Response

 2   The commission adopts commenters’ recommendation to require a large load customer to

 3   pay transmission rates based on the demand that the large load customer places on the

 4   ERCOT system. However, the commission determines that the details of the charge should

 5   be decided in Project No. 58000. Accordingly, the commission modifies the adopted rule to

 6   require the SLLIA include a term of acknowledgment and agreement that the large load

 7   customer will pay the large load minimum billing demand described in §25.193, relating to

 8   Distribution Service Provider Transmission Cost Recovery Factor (TCRF), for the set period

 9   of time described in §25.193. The commission also modifies the adopted rule to include the

10   large load minimum billing demand in the list identifying what constitutes an outstanding

11   amount owed and modifies the adopted rule to specify that a large load customer may be

Commission staff's recommended adoption order would adopt new 16 Texas Administrative
Code (TAC) §25.194, relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards.

        The purpose of the new rule is to implement Public Utility Regulatory Act §37.0561, as
enacted by Senate Bill 6 during the Texas 89th Legislature, Regular Session. Commission
Staff's recommended adoption order requires a large load customer, before the large load
customer can be included in an ERCOT interconnection study, to execute an intermediate
agreement, provide certain disclosures, and post financial security in the amount $50,000 per
megawatt. The new rule also requires a large load customer to execute a standard large load
agreement, update its disclosures, post financial security, and pay contribution in aid of
construction for direct interconnection costs. Additionally, the new rule sets forth the
consequences of withdrawing all or a portion of requested peak demand or contracted peak demand
and the consequences for providing false or inaccurate information. Finally, the new rule sets forth
the terms for the return of financial security to a large load customer that energizes.

        Commission Staff recommends the Commission adopt the order attached to this
memorandum.

Commission Response

The commission declines to adopt Cloud HQ and DCC recommendations to strike the
provision setting forth the requirements for non-utilized transmission capacity, and declines
Skybox’s recommendation to defer the development of rules for non-utilized transmission

capacity to a subsequent proceeding.

The commission’s modification of the adopted rule to require that the SLLIA include an
acknowledgement and agreement that the large load customer will pay the large load
minimum billing demand mitigates risk to ratepayers associated with delayed energization.
However, permitting a large load customer to indefinitely reserve transmission capacity
without utilizing it would foreclose other customers from interconnecting to a system that
has been planned and built to serve demand that has not materialized. This outcome would
be contrary to both aspects of the Legislature’s direction under PURA §37.0561 to support
business development and minimize the potential for stranded infrastructure costs.
Moreover, PURA §37.0561 directs the commission to establish uniform standards addressing

the circumstances under which transmission capacity subject to an outstanding financial
